title: Intraday time series momentum: Global evidence and links to market characteristics
one_line: The first half-hour return predicts the last half-hour return in 12 of 16 developed markets (2005-2017); the effect is stronger in crises, recessions and illiquid periods; out-of-sample it beats the historical mean in 14 of 16 markets but R² is positive in only 5; returns are before costs.

findings.statement: Pooled first-half-hour coefficient 2.86 (t = 7.53); significant in 12 of 16 markets in-sample.
US predictability concentrated in the financial crisis (scaled coefficient 18.3 vs 4.3 outside).
Strategy returns roughly double in low-liquidity periods; stronger when information arrives smoothly (frog-in-the-pan).
Country strategies alpha 2.7-7.5%/yr gross; no transaction costs deducted.

why.pattern: Late-informed traders and hedgers rebalancing near the close; liquidity-dependent.

tradable_edge: Already covered by the Gao et al. first-half-hour → last-half-hour logic inside noise_area_last_half_hour_es; adds a split to run: by volatility regime (crisis-type days) — the effect may live only in high-volatility tercile.
angles: Report last-30 strategy by AvgRange tercile

decay_risk.reason: US effect mostly 2008-2009; gross returns only.

data_fit: ES 1-min Dec 2013 → Sep 2026, NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026 (2024+ protected in the backtest project).
